# ISSUE-30 implementation plan

Derive network access from saved progress and use it to gate DEEP FIELD's existing SECOND LINE board. The maintenance-panel puzzle and Relay Trivia will grant the same access independently once DEEP FIELD is available. A fixture will exercise a trade receipt through the existing door host. Reuse the released archive and SYSOP response to demonstrate what earned research and reputation do.

The WorkUnit specifies `multi_area` and the approved `detailed` profile. Advisory estimates for the remaining dimensions are `known` uncertainty and `standard` risk. Allow roughly 6–12 hours for planning, review, implementation and validation within the 32-hour claim budget in `.swarm/active/SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`. Issue dependencies #27 and #28 are listed in `.swarm/active/workunit.json`. The mounted tree has the door host, reward, message-read events and scripted dialogue this design needs.

## What we know

- V2 saves have a nullable `profile.accessLevel`. Fresh saves and migrated v1 saves set it to null, and hub `STATUS` only shows it if set. The legacy lift preserves the actual progress arrays, and `factsOf` already exposes their flags and completions. The completed v1 fixture includes the optional `service-panel-open` fact. [src/progress/save.ts:48](../../src/progress/save.ts#L48) · [src/progress/save.ts:172](../../src/progress/save.ts#L172) · [src/progress/save.ts:235](../../src/progress/save.ts#L235) · [src/main.ts:99](../../src/main.ts#L99) · [tests/fixtures/episode-000-complete-v1.json:2](../../tests/fixtures/episode-000-complete-v1.json#L2)
- The maintenance panel is playable through the map and grants `flag:service-panel-open`. The first door grants `flag:relay-trivia-complete`, and its host persists the reward and checkpoint before copying them back to live data. Each producer requires Episode 000 completion, which is also the existing DEEP FIELD entry condition. [src/app/tools.ts:113](../../src/app/tools.ts#L113) · [content/puzzles/service-panel.json:5](../../content/puzzles/service-panel.json#L5) · [content/doors/relay-trivia.json:8](../../content/doors/relay-trivia.json#L8) · [src/doors/host.ts:83](../../src/doors/host.ts#L83) · [content/bbs/deep-field.json:5](../../content/bbs/deep-field.json#L5)
- The current SECOND LINE board is listed and enterable without an access check. Its only thread links `community.second-line`, whose condition also applies in the hub archive. A board gate by itself would open an empty board to the door-only player. [src/bbs/bbs.ts:197](../../src/bbs/bbs.ts#L197) · [src/bbs/bbs.ts:279](../../src/bbs/bbs.ts#L279) · [src/bbs/bbs.ts:564](../../src/bbs/bbs.ts#L564) · [content/bbs/second-line-thread.json:7](../../content/bbs/second-line-thread.json#L7) · [content/community/first-light.json:23](../../content/community/first-light.json#L23) · [src/puzzle/game.ts:112](../../src/puzzle/game.ts#L112)
- The relay note read settles a flag already used by a higher-priority SYSOP response. Existing dialogue tests exercise the baseline and the response. `loadContent` checks condition references after flattening community packages, and the build, CLI and bundled client share it. [content/events/relay-read.json:2](../../content/events/relay-read.json#L2) · [content/characters/sysop.json:13](../../content/characters/sysop.json#L13) · [src/narrative/dialogue.ts:24](../../src/narrative/dialogue.ts#L24) · [tests/unit/bbs.test.ts:239](../../tests/unit/bbs.test.ts#L239) · [src/content/validate.ts:123](../../src/content/validate.ts#L123) · [src/content/browser.ts:3](../../src/content/browser.ts#L3) · [scripts/content-plugin.ts:7](../../scripts/content-plugin.ts#L7)
- Typed BBS commands and native buttons share the same dispatcher. A rejected board command can keep the current route, emit `restricted` tone, and omit the effect. The door host supplies live facts and the door session re-enters the signed-in menu on exit. [src/bbs/bbs-view.ts:29](../../src/bbs/bbs-view.ts#L29) · [src/terminal/terminal.ts:77](../../src/terminal/terminal.ts#L77) · [src/terminal/terminal.ts:118](../../src/terminal/terminal.ts#L118) · [src/doors/host.ts:111](../../src/doors/host.ts#L111) · [src/bbs/door-session.ts:32](../../src/bbs/door-session.ts#L32)

## What we're assuming

- Use `VISITOR` for the default level and `RELAY` for SECOND LINE. These are interface labels for Episode 000's existing content. The future story's `MAINTAINER` label and its progression remain governed by `docs/game-design.md:140`. Confirm naming and the choice of SECOND LINE at the plan review.
- SECOND LINE's existing post should be available through both earned routes wherever the shared archive condition is evaluated. The proposed data change extends the hub archive listing to Relay Trivia graduates as well. Confirm the intended scope at plan review and exercise both surfaces in focused tests.
- Existing v2 payloads can be read after removing the unused rank field. Confirm with a v2 payload containing an old rank string and another with the field absent, preserving the original profile and progress apart from the obsolete field. The completed v1 fixture should derive RELAY because it already has the service-panel fact. Derive VISITOR for a copy with the optional panel progress removed.

## Open questions

- Actual browser interaction and save persistence under Chromium remain to be observed in the existing Linux `Browser tests` CI job. This planner's browser capability is denied. Step 5 supplies browser coverage for all required inputs and a Node route check for earlier verification.
- The WorkUnit specifies no additional harness or OS. The configured runtime path for role checks is Linux, SwarmOS isolated/native with the Codex developer/tester harnesses (`.swarm/config.yaml:4`, `:16`, `:59`–`:67`). The production runtime exercised by CI is Linux hosted Actions, Playwright Chromium, with bundled static assets intercepted under `/signal-lost/` (`.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml:11`–`:25`, `playwright.config.ts:3`–`:16`, `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts:16`–`:37`). Other OS and browser combinations have no WorkUnit coverage requirement.
- The mounted source has no accessible Git metadata. New file paths were checked against the supplied approved-source snapshot. Confirm them against the coordinator's candidate base when its Git identity is available.

## Implementation sequence

1. **Content and pure derivation.** In `src/content/schema.ts`, add `accessLevelSchema`, `capabilitySchema`, typed records and the `Content.accessLevels` / `Content.capabilities` arrays. Define each access record with a stable ID, label, nonnegative integer rank and optional `when`. Use the existing fact syntax, including read-only BBS read facts in conditions, with a recursive access-only schema admitting fact leaves and nonempty `all` / `any` groups. Require exactly one unconditional rank 0 in any nonempty level catalog and a condition on every positive rank. Reject duplicate ranks alongside existing duplicate-ID and unknown-fact diagnostics. In new pure `src/progress/access.ts`, implement `deriveAccessLevel(levels, facts)` for the highest qualifying rank and `hasAccessLevel(levels, current, requiredId)` for threshold comparison. Empty catalogs are valid for content subsets with no board gate and produce no level. Unrecognized thresholds fail closed. Positive grammar plus maximum selection makes every valid catalog monotonic as facts accumulate. Keep normal condition syntax for existing consumers.
2. **Author existing sources and consumers.** Add `content/access-levels/visitor.json` (rank 0) and `content/access-levels/relay.json` (rank 1, `any` of the service-panel and first-door flags). Add optional `access: { level, deniedText }` to `bbsMessageBoardSchema` and author a RELAY requirement with a line such as `SECOND LINE SWITCHBOARD: CARRIER HELD. RELAY CLEARANCE REQUIRED.` in `content/bbs/second-line.json`. Give the existing `community.second-line` archive in `content/community/first-light.json` the same two fact alternatives in its `requires`; keep the transmission's existing condition. Add `content/capabilities/service-panel-research.json` and `content/capabilities/relay-desk-reputation.json`, declaring the existing `flag:service-panel-open` and `flag:relay-note-read` with the archive and SYSOP response as their respective uses. The declarations refer to facts already earned through the puzzle and read-event flows, with no counters or new persisted fields.
3. **Validate a capability's effect.** Register the two JSON directories in `SCHEMAS` and initialize their arrays in `loadContent` in `src/content/validate.ts`. Use existing loader references and diagnostics, including for minimum-level IDs. A capability holds a saved fact, a concrete target, and optional `context` facts for evaluating the target (default empty). Research targets are an archive ID or a gated BBS message-board ID. Reputation targets identify a character and BBS line. Validate referenced facts with the existing vocabulary and producer checks, reject a context containing its own capability fact, and resolve targets after community flattening. For an archive, use `evaluate` to require false with only context and true with the capability fact added. For a board, require the equivalent threshold transition via `deriveAccessLevel` and `hasAccessLevel`. For reputation, resolve a character reachable through SYSOP or TALK, use `createScriptedDialogue` for BBS with empty seen/failure state in both cases, and require the advertised line to become the selected response with different visible text. Reject unknown targets, incapable gates and unchanged or shadowed responses at the declaration's target field. This is a concrete proof at the supplied fact context. The shipped cases separately prove that context and rewards occur through normal play. Document the fields after the existing condition example in `docs/content-authoring.md`.
4. **Wire the save and UI entry points.** Remove the obsolete profile member from `saveSchema`, `freshSave` and `loadSave`'s legacy conversion in `src/progress/save.ts`. Keep schema version 2 and use the existing Zod object stripping for old ranks when parsed and on subsequent writes. The v1 lift still preserves all facts, and localStorage remains the only save source. In `src/main.ts`, evaluate the derived level on every STATUS invocation using current `game.facts()`. Share the authored `ACCESS LEVEL: {level}` format with the BBS using `bbsCopy.text.accessLevel` in `content/bbs/interface.json` and `bbsInterfaceSchema`. In `src/bbs/bbs.ts`, pass the level records through `getBbsOffer` and derive the live level for `menu` and for the `BOARD <id>` branch of `dispatch`. Keep the locked board's usual button and HELP command available so activating it gives feedback. Below threshold return the authored `restricted` output, stay in BOARDS, and emit no entry or read effect. Successful entry calls existing `showBoard` and the existing history path. THREAD and REPLY already require the in-board routes. Leave the connect prerequisite and post conditions in place. Existing `createBbsDoorSession`, `createBbsScene` and `createTerminal` carry both input modes and re-render the menu from committed facts on exit.
5. **Add and verify focused cases.** Add `tests/unit/access.test.ts` with a level/rank table, monotonic superset cases and inline isolation fixtures for a solved puzzle and a once-only trade receipt. Use `createGame.attempt` for the puzzle and a test-only code-door registration with `createDoorHost` for the trade. Persist and reopen each route through the save API. Extend the existing content, BBS, save and browser suites per TEST_PLAN.md. Browser cases start with Episode 000 complete and optional panel progress removed, prove denial through both input modes, earn the real first door reward, and verify access in that session and after reload. Keep a separate test assertion for the original v1 fixture, which begins at RELAY.

# ISSUE-30 test plan

## Acceptance coverage

The criteria below follow `.swarm/active/WORKUNIT.md:26–30`. Run the focused Node checks on Linux under the configured SwarmOS isolated/native Codex environment. The browser cases exercise the bundled static game and real localStorage in Linux CI Chromium through the existing production-build fixture.

| # | Acceptance criterion | Cases and observable result | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A table-driven test shows level derivation for fact sets including each route, and that levels are never lost when more facts arrive | In `tests/unit/access.test.ts`, load the shipped JSON for cases with no facts, completed episode only, unrelated facts, only the panel reward, only the door reward, and both rewards. Expect VISITOR for the first three and RELAY for each qualifying route. Test supersets that add unrelated facts, BBS reads and the other route, and a fixture whose extra tier becomes eligible later. Compare numeric ranks and verify minimum-level checks accept the higher level. Vary catalog/fact order. `tests/unit/content.test.ts` rejects a nested negation, empty groups, a missing baseline, duplicate rank, invalid rank/condition pairing and an unknown leaf/board threshold. | D1, D2 |
| 2 | A test using fixtures shows a puzzle-only route and a trading-only route each reaching the required level with no facts from the other | In `tests/unit/access.test.ts`, use the real loader with inline JSON for a baseline and a required tier conditioned on the fixture puzzle's solved fact or the fixture trade receipt. Use two fresh saves with identical common prerequisites and start below the tier. In one, solve the fixture via `createGame.attempt`; in the other, complete one exchange in a test-only code-door fixture through `createDoorHost` and earn the declared receipt. Confirm that an incorrect/unfinished action does not advance either save. Compare newly added route facts exactly, exclude the other producer's facts, and assert that each save still reaches the same tier after reopen. Keep fixture puzzle and trading code in the test tree. | D1 |
| 3 | A restricted area denies entry with diegetic text below its level, and opens at its level, by keyboard and pointer | In `tests/unit/bbs.test.ts`, sign in with VISITOR, check the SECOND LINE action is present, issue `BOARD second-line` and assert the authored restricted line, unchanged BOARDS phase and no history/read effect. Direct THREAD cannot bypass the board. Gain the service fact and retry without recreating the BBS. Assert board entry, the existing thread and its attribution. In `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts`, use a v1 save copy with Episode 000 complete and optional panel progress removed. Parameterize keyboard and pointer. In the keyboard case, submit a typed command and use keyboard focus/Enter on the native board button. In the pointer case, use the same button with a click. Assert that the latest restricted output contains the authored line and the thread action is absent. Complete the existing Relay Trivia door using its declared answers and assert RELAY on return to the signed-in menu. Enter SECOND LINE by the same input mode and read the existing credited post. Reconnect after reload and verify access still works. The door-only path contains no service grant. | D1 for routing and effects. C1 for browser controls, visible text and reload. |

Reject research with no resolvable target, an always-visible archive, an archive that stays locked with the capability fact, or an ineffective board threshold. Add a valid board-target case and verify fact reference/context errors. Reject reputation with no change in selected response, including an always-active target, a flag that merely appears in status, a shadowed higher-priority response, or identical output. Check diagnostics with the declaration file and field. In `tests/unit/access.test.ts`, solve the real service puzzle after seeding shared Episode 000 progress and verify the archive appears through `game.archives()`. Verify the door flag alternative also makes the same archive available. In `tests/unit/bbs.test.ts`, reuse the relay note read → event → SYSOP flow and show the baseline and the authored changed line; confirm the reputation flag is independent of elevated access. | D1, D2 |
| 5 | `STATUS` and the BBS show the level, and a migrated version 1 save derives the correct starting level | In `tests/unit/save.test.ts`, migrate the original v1 fixture to V2 and derive RELAY from the preserved panel flag. Migrate the below-threshold variant and derive VISITOR. Test legacy v2 payloads with a stale higher string and with the field absent, preserving other save data and showing the rank is absent on write. Extend `tests/e2e/progress.spec.ts` to assert fresh STATUS displays VISITOR alongside the existing link text, an old v2 cache does not override facts, and handle normalization and literal rendering still work. Extend the original migrated case in `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts` to assert RELAY in hub STATUS and the signed-in BBS menu before the door. ## Tester independent review and reuse

- Review the candidate diff against each criterion and the approved scope. Follow real producers through persistence and the same fact set into STATUS, BBS menu, board dispatch, archives and dialogue. Verify the fixture sources are independent, the access-only condition schema enforces positive predicates, the capability checks exercise the actual consumers, and the BBS denial path leaves route and progress intact.
- Review browser assertions for fresh navigation, native activation, denial, unlock and persistence. The browser proof belongs to C1. Report which runtime assertions remain outstanding if CI has yet to run on the candidate.
- Reuse applicable D1–D5 passes from `IMPLEMENTATION.md` with a criterion-specific evidence reference in `.swarm/active/VALIDATION.md`. Use source/fixture/dependency identity and changed paths to assess applicability. A relevant source change, observed failure or unresolved coverage concern warrants the smallest applicable rerun from D1–D5. For example, `npm test -- tests/unit/access.test.ts tests/unit/save.test.ts` can address a migration or fact-derivation gap. Record the reason and source identity for any rerun. Treat absent results or unresolved applicability as unverified and follow the active tester contract for the machine-readable acceptance record.
- Agent results are advisory. The coordinator's claim-bound validation and the CI browser result supply their own evidence.

## Coordinator policy and longer checks

Times are scheduling estimates. The coordinator runs the complete trusted-base policy once on the final candidate after the roles finish and before publication. `.swarm/validation/required-checks.yaml:1–13` is its reference for `format`, `lint`, `build` and `test`, using Node's prepared/offline dependency setup. The existing Browser tests workflow supplies the interaction and browser persistence evidence required before merge.

| V1 | Final claim-bound `swarm issue validate 30`, applying the full trusted-base format, lint, build and unit-test policy to the final candidate | coordinator | 6–15 min for policy plus dependency preparation. The unit policy entry is allowed up to 15 min on its own. | Coordinator validation report in `.swarm/active/VALIDATION.md` and required-check logs for the bound candidate and approved base/policy identity. Publication and review reuse the bound report for that candidate. Prior focused role passes support acceptance review. |

In the same CI-capable Linux environment, the relevant focused diagnostic is `npm run test:e2e -- tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts tests/e2e/progress.spec.ts`. | CI | 6–15 min including setup, build and suite execution.
